page_hint: Chapter 26 §3 Pattern A / §8 Step 0 / Fig 26.1 caption
quoted_clause: The canonical scenario's short-prompt workload — the RAG anchor — rendered as a six-axis fingerprint. The three scored workload families from the §26.2.1 matrix — long-context RAG Q&A, high-throughput chat, and batch inference — sit in distinct regions
observed: Fig 26.1 is described as rendering the canonical short-prompt RAG workload, but the plotted RAG family is long-context RAG Q&A (context score 0.95). Step 0 then says the capstone short-prompt workload 'deliberately matches none of the three families plotted in Fig 26.1.' These statements cannot all be true.
evidence: The figure provenance note gives long-context RAG Q&A a context score of 0.95, while the canonical scenario is repeatedly described as short-prompt (<2K input) and Step 1 says it is 'not the canonical 9.2K-input/1.08-s-prefill case.' The caption nevertheless calls the figure the canonical short-prompt RAG anchor.
root_cause: The figure was likely built from the long-context RAG row of the matrix but captioned as the canonical short-prompt RAG anchor; Step 0 was then written against the actual plotted families.
correction: Either plot the short-prompt RAG Q&A family (with a low context-length score consistent with <2K input) and keep the canonical-anchor caption, or relabel Fig 26.1 as a long-context RAG/chat/batch fingerprint and remove the claim that it renders the canonical short-prompt workload. Update Step 0 so it does not contradict the figure.
acceptance_test: Fig 26.1 caption, provenance note, plotted scores, and §8 Step 0 all identify the same workload family; the canonical short-prompt RAG workload is either the plotted RAG family or explicitly excluded from the figure.

quoted_clause: Deeper continuous batching on the single host, on top of the baseline sharding, cannot raise throughput here: resident-request capacity is KV-bound at C ≈ 17.5 (Ch 15), so admitting more requests only lengthens the waiting queue and adds prefill interference
observed: The argument treats the KV-resident concurrency ceiling C ≈ 17.5 as if the baseline already operates at that ceiling. A KV ceiling bounds steady-state resident requests; it does not by itself prove that deeper continuous batching cannot raise throughput from a lower baseline batch size up to C.
evidence: Throughput can rise as batch size increases toward the KV-capacity limit even when C is fixed. The claim is only valid once the scheduler is already at C; otherwise deeper batching can improve utilization and throughput before queueing dominates. The text does not state that the baseline is already at C.
root_cause: Capacity ceiling conflated with current operating point.
correction: Qualify the claim: 'once the scheduler is already at the KV-resident ceiling C ≈ 17.5, deeper batching cannot raise steady-state concurrency further; below C it may raise throughput until queueing and prefill interference dominate.' If the capstone assumes the baseline is already at C, state that assumption explicitly.
acceptance_test: The passage distinguishes the KV capacity ceiling from the baseline operating batch/concurrency and states the condition under which deeper batching cannot help.

page_hint: Chapter 26 Table 26-2 cost row and following note
quoted_clause: Cost | $ per query — metered API spend at the canonical 9,200/300 mix, marginal-generation-work share only (DERIVED from FACT inputs, §26.8 — not itself a FACT) | < $0.015 | $0.0076 (API-basis marginal: canonical-mix unit price $0.01164 — a conservative upper bound for this short-prompt leg — × 0.65; self-host all-in is a separate basis, §26.8)
observed: The row mixes two cost bases: 'metered API spend' and 'marginal-generation-work share only.' Multiplying an API unit price by 0.65 produces an API-spend estimate, not a self-hosted marginal-generation-work estimate. The note then calls the modeled cell a marginal-generation-work statement.
evidence: The arithmetic $0.01164 × 0.65 = $0.007566 is an API-basis per-request spend after a 35% cache-hit reduction. It is not the same quantity as self-hosted marginal generation work. The note says the cell is a marginal-generation-work statement, but the cell's inputs are API list prices.
root_cause: Cost-basis labels were carried over from the self-host discussion into an API-priced row.
correction: Either label the row explicitly as 'API-basis marginal spend after cache-hit reduction' and remove 'marginal-generation-work share only,' or compute a separate self-hosted marginal-generation-work figure and keep the API-basis figure in a separate row/column. Do not describe the API-priced cell as a marginal-generation-work estimate.
acceptance_test: The cost row's label, arithmetic, and note all name the same basis; API spend and self-hosted marginal generation work are not conflated.

evidence: The table has four rows. The prose says 'three registers' and 'three kinds of statement.'
root_cause: A fourth register was added without updating the heading and count.

page_hint: Appendix A post-snapshot notes, multiple paragraphs
observed: Multiple footnote clusters contain stray caret-comma-caret sequences between footnote references, e.g. `[^oct-mt-huginn]^,^[^oct-mt-ouro]`, `[^oct-mt-ouro-code]^,^[^oct-mt-ouro-card]`, and similar patterns in the Intel and video notes.
evidence: The pattern appears repeatedly in the manuscript chunk. It is not standard Markdown footnote syntax and is likely to render as stray superscript punctuation or break footnote parsing.
root_cause: Mechanical insertion or conversion artifact between adjacent footnote references.
correction: Replace each `]^,^[` pattern with a clean separator, e.g. `][^...]` or `]; [^...]`, according to the book's footnote style. Search globally for `^,^`.
acceptance_test: No `^,^` sequences remain; adjacent footnote references render cleanly in the built PDF.

quoted_clause: the Qwen figure is a backbone-only ratio, not a fraction of the deployed parameter inventory; the table is offloadable
observed: The phrase 'the table is offloadable' is ambiguous in context: 'table' refers to Qwen's N-gram embedding table, but the sentence sits near references to the book's tables and the Fig A.1 table.
evidence: The antecedent is separated from the phrase by a long parenthetical and the word 'table' is used elsewhere in the appendix for data tables.
correction: Replace with 'the N-gram embedding table is offloadable' or 'those embedding tables are offloadable.'
acceptance_test: A reader can identify the offloadable object without reconstructing the antecedent from the preceding parenthetical.
